metadata.title: IR band map for CO2 hydrogenation
metadata.description: Approximate band positions for surface and gas-phase species in CO₂ hydrogenation. Exact positions depend on support, coverage, and reaction conditions. The asterisk (*) denotes a surface-bound species.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ asymmetric stretch (νₐₛ) — R-branch (ΔJ = +1) at ~2360 cm⁻¹. Higher-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the P-branch at ~2335. Q-branch forbidden (Σ→Σ transition), leaving a characteristic gap at the band origin. Saturates at high pressure.

references.note: Reports the ν₃ (our νₐₛ) band origin (00011←00001) at 2349 cm⁻¹ (Table 2); ~2360 here is the R-branch envelope maximum, not a measured peak.
Table 3: gas-phase CO₂ R-branch at 2373 cm⁻¹ observed during DRM at 600°C; used as reactant concentration marker.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ asymmetric stretch (νₐₛ) — P-branch (ΔJ = −1) at ~2335 cm⁻¹. Lower-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the R-branch at ~2360. Q-branch forbidden (Σ→Σ transition). Saturates at high pressure.

references.note: Reports the ν₃ (our νₐₛ) band origin (00011←00001) at 2349 cm⁻¹ (Table 2); ~2335 here is the P-branch envelope maximum, not a measured peak.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ bending fundamental (δ) — R-branch (ΔJ = +1) at ~700 cm⁻¹. Higher-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the P-branch at ~660. Q-branch is allowed (Σ→Π transition) and appears as a sharp spike at ~667 between P and R envelopes.

references.note: Reports the ν₂ (our δ) band origin (01101←00001) at 667 cm⁻¹ (Table 2); ~700 here is the R-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ bending fundamental (δ) — Q-branch (ΔJ = 0) at ~667 cm⁻¹. Sharp, intense spike between P and R envelopes; allowed because this mode is a Σ→Π (perpendicular) transition. Saturates very quickly at modest pCO₂.

references.note: Q-branch coincides with the reported ν₂ (our δ) band origin (01101←00001) at 667 cm⁻¹ (Table 2) — the fundamental bending mode.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ bending fundamental (δ) — P-branch (ΔJ = −1) at ~660 cm⁻¹. Lower-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the R-branch at ~700. Atmospheric CO₂ in the beam path contributes to this region; routinely seen even with good purging.

references.note: Reports the ν₂ (our δ) band origin (01101←00001) at 667 cm⁻¹ (Table 2); ~660 here is the P-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ combination band at ~3730 cm⁻¹; (νₛ + νₐₛ) R-branch — upper Fermi-resonance component, R-side. Useful for high-pressure quantification when the νₐₛ fundamental saturates.

references.note: Reports the (ν₁+ν₃) [our νₛ+νₐₛ] band origin (10011←00001) at ~3715 cm⁻¹ (Table 2, upper Fermi-resonance pair); ~3730 here is the R-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ combination band at ~3699 cm⁻¹; (νₛ + νₐₛ) P-branch — upper Fermi-resonance component, P-side. P/R-branch separation ~30 cm⁻¹; pair-mate of the R-branch at ~3730.

references.note: Reports the (ν₁+ν₃) [our νₛ+νₐₛ] band origin (10011←00001) at ~3715 cm⁻¹ (Table 2, upper Fermi-resonance pair); ~3699 here is the P-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ combination band at ~3627 cm⁻¹; (2δ + νₐₛ) R-branch — lower Fermi-resonance component, R-side. Separation between Fermi pair (3730 vs 3627) ~107 cm⁻¹ is fixed.

references.note: Reports the (2ν₂+ν₃) [our 2δ+νₐₛ] band origin (10012←00001) at ~3613 cm⁻¹ (Table 2, lower Fermi-resonance pair); ~3627 here is the R-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ combination band at ~3597 cm⁻¹; (2δ + νₐₛ) P-branch — lower Fermi-resonance component, P-side. P/R-branch separation ~30 cm⁻¹; pair-mate of the R-branch at ~3627.

references.note: Reports the (2ν₂+ν₃) [our 2δ+νₐₛ] band origin (10012←00001) at ~3613 cm⁻¹ (Table 2, lower Fermi-resonance pair); ~3597 here is the P-branch envelope maximum.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ combination band at ~2077 cm⁻¹; (11101 ← 00001) Q-branch — the most intense combination band in the 2200–1900 cm⁻¹ region. Falls in the typical metal-carbonyl stretching range and has been repeatedly misassigned in DRIFTS studies of Cu-based methanol synthesis catalysts as ν(CO) on Cu(0)/Cu(111)/low-index Cu planes. Intensity grows with CO₂ pressure and temperature. Always check for this band before assigning a 2077 cm⁻¹ feature to surface CO.

references.note: Table 3, band J: very strong, narrow Q-branch (11101←00001, ¹²C¹⁶O₂) — most intense combination band in the investigated range; used as the intensity-normalization reference (no temperature dependence). Particularly pronounced in their long-path-length Praying Mantis HTRC cell; intensity amplified at elevated CO₂ pressures.

bands.description: Gas CO₂ symmetric stretch (νₛ) band origin at ~1388 cm⁻¹. Strictly IR-forbidden by symmetry (Σg⁺ — centrosymmetric, no dipole moment change); observed only in Raman spectroscopy. Listed here as the explicit parent mode for the νₛ+νₐₛ combination band (~3715 cm⁻¹) and as the Fermi-resonance partner of 2δ (~1334 cm⁻¹).

references.note: ν₁ (our νₛ) band origin (Table 2); IR-inactive (Σg⁺) — included for context as the Fermi-dyad partner of 2ν₂ (our 2δ) and parent of the (ν₁+ν₃) [our νₛ+νₐₛ] combination band.

bands.description: Gas-phase CO stretch (ν) — R-branch (ΔJ = +1) at ~2170 cm⁻¹. Higher-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the P-branch at ~2115. Q-branch forbidden for diatomic CO (Σ→Σ transition), leaving a characteristic gap at ~2143 cm⁻¹ between R and P branches.

references.note: R-branch of CO rotovibrational spectrum clearly visible at 2176 cm⁻¹ (Figs. 4–6). Band shape and width are temperature-dependent: higher T broadens the envelope via Maxwell–Boltzmann redistribution of rotational populations. Accurate gas-phase subtraction requires a SiC reference spectrum collected under identical gas composition and temperature.

bands.description: Gas-phase CO stretch (ν) — P-branch (ΔJ = −1) at ~2115 cm⁻¹. Lower-frequency rotational envelope; pair-mate of the R-branch at ~2170. P/R splitting ~55 cm⁻¹ at room temperature; envelope broadens and shifts intensity to higher-J lines as temperature increases (Maxwell–Boltzmann redistribution).

references.note: P-branch of CO rotovibrational spectrum at 2114 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 4). P/R splitting ~62 cm⁻¹ (2176−2114 cm⁻¹). Temperature-dependent lineshape; imperfect background correction using a SiC reference at the wrong temperature leaves a spurious positive artefact near 2220 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 5d–e).

bands.description: Gas methane asymmetric C-H stretch (νₐₛ, T₂ mode); sharp Q-branch at ~3019 cm⁻¹ with rotational P/R structure.

references.note: Table 3: νs(–CH₃) at 3016 cm⁻¹; gas-phase CH₄ C-H stretch during DRM at 600°C over Ni-Ce-Fe/La-Al₂O₃.

bands.description: Gas methane asymmetric bending (δₐₛ, T₂ mode) at ~1306 cm⁻¹.

references.note: Table 3: ν(CH₄, Gaseous) at 1306 cm⁻¹; present across all catalysts under DRM at 600°C; gas-phase CH₄ concentration marker.

bands.description: Gas methane symmetric bending (δₛ, E mode) at ~1534 cm⁻¹. IR-forbidden by symmetry (E in Td — no T₂ component); observed only in Raman spectroscopy. Listed here as the explicit parent mode for the δₛ+νₐₛ combination band (~4220 cm⁻¹).
Gas methane combination band at ~4220 cm⁻¹; useful for high-pressure quantification when νₐₛ saturates. Often outside standard DRIFTS window.

Linear (atop) CO bonded to a single metal atom. Most common adsorption mode on Cu, Pt, Pd, Rh, Ni, and Co surfaces. Frequency depends on metal identity, oxidation state, coordination environment, and surface coverage due to π-backdonation and dipole coupling. Typical values: Cu⁰ ~2080–2100, Pt ~2070, Rh ~2050 cm⁻¹. Electron-poor or partially oxidized sites shift to higher frequency.

references.note: Linear (on-top) CO on metallic Co at 2041 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 5a, Section 3.3). 14% Co/Siralox shows cobalt carbonyl signal spanning 2100–1700 cm⁻¹ with maximum at ~2059 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 4c, Section 3.2). Gas-phase CO R/P branches at 2176/2114 cm⁻¹ are simultaneously visible and must be subtracted; ill-resolved bridged/multibonded CO bands appear below 2000 cm⁻¹.

Linear ¹²CO on Pt at the Pt–CeO₂ interface at 2053 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 4a); red-shifted by ~20–30 cm⁻¹ from bare Pt (2070–2080 cm⁻¹) due to enhanced π-backdonation from highly reduced CeO₂. SSITKA confirms this species is an active intermediate in RWGS: isotopic exchange rate matches CO(g) production rate. Under ¹³CO₂ a further red-shift to 2005 cm⁻¹ is observed, consistent with the expected isotopic shift for a linear CO stretch.

bands.description: Bridging CO coordinated between two metal atoms. Lower frequency than linear CO due to increased metal→CO π-backdonation from multiple metal centers. Common on Pt, Pd, Rh, Ni, and Co surfaces; less common on Cu and typically observed only at high coverage or defect sites. Often associated with step and edge sites.

references.note: Ill-resolved bands below 2000 cm⁻¹ on Co/Al₂O₃ attributed to bridged and multibonded CO (Fig. 5a, Section 3.3); not separately resolved from the dominant linear CO band at 2041 cm⁻¹. Appear as a broad shoulder below the linear CO feature.

bands.description: Three-fold hollow CO coordinated to three metal atoms. Common on close-packed Pt, Pd, Rh, and Ni surfaces at moderate-to-high CO coverage. Rare on Cu surfaces. Stronger multi-center π-backdonation shifts ν(CO) to lower frequency than bridge or linear adsorption.

Four-fold hollow CO coordinated to four metal atoms. Rare adsorption geometry reported mainly on Ni(100), Co, and related surfaces. Exhibits the lowest ν(CO) frequencies among metal–CO adsorption modes due to strong multi-center π-backdonation.

Linear CO adsorbed on Lewis-acidic metal cation sites of oxide supports, zeolites, or isolated metal centers. Reduced metal→CO π-backdonation shifts ν(CO) to higher frequency than on metallic surfaces. Typical values: Cu⁺ ~2100–2130, Cu²⁺ ~2150–2180, Ce³⁺ ~2130, Ce⁴⁺ ~2160, Ti⁴⁺ ~2190, Zn²⁺ ~2200, and Al³⁺/Mg²⁺ ~2210 cm⁻¹. Widely used as a probe of Lewis acidity and oxidation state.

Isocarbonyl species with CO coordinated through oxygen rather than carbon (M–OC). Rare adsorption mode observed on highly oxidized surfaces, strongly electrophilic cations, and certain zeolite environments. Typically exhibits higher ν(CO) frequency than conventional C-bound carbonyls.

asymmetric ν(CO) component of geminal dicarbonyl species with two linear CO ligands bound to a single isolated cationic metal center, typically Rh⁺, Ir⁺, Ru⁺, or Cu⁺. The symmetric/asymmetric pair is diagnostic of atomically dispersed cationic sites. Typical splitting: ~50–60 cm⁻¹.

Symmetric ν(CO) component of geminal dicarbonyl species with two linear CO ligands bound to a single isolated cationic metal center. Appears together with the asymmetric band and is characteristic of isolated cationic adsorption sites.
Surface formyl C=O stretch (HCO*); mechanistic intermediate from CO + H. Often observed transiently. Distinguishes the CO-H pathway from formate-mediated routes.
Formyl C-H stretch (HCO*); lower than formate ν(CH) at ~2870-2900 and weaker. Diagnostic when paired with C=O at ~1750.
Adsorbed formaldehyde C=O stretch (H₂CO*); reduction product of formyl. Key methanol precursor in some mechanisms.
Adsorbed formaldehyde CH₂ asymmetric stretch (H₂CO*).
Adsorbed formaldehyde CH₂ symmetric stretch (H₂CO*).
Adsorbed formaldehyde CH₂ scissoring (H₂CO*); overlaps monodentate carbonate νₐₛ.
Generic surface acyl/aldehyde C=O stretch (R-C=O*); broad assignment used when species cannot be specifically identified. Distinguishes from formate by absence of ν(CH) at ~2870.
Hydroxymethyl O-H stretch (H₂COH*); late methanol precursor. Often masked by surface OH.
Hydroxymethyl CH₂ stretch (H₂COH*); overlaps methoxy and methanol.
Hydroxymethyl C-O stretch (H₂COH*); overlaps methoxy ν(C-O) at ~1050-1100.
Bidentate carbonate asymmetric stretch (b-CO₃²⁻*); large splitting (Δν ~300 cm⁻¹).

references.note: Table 3: νas(-C=O) 1670 + νas(OCO⁻) 1560 + νs(OCO⁻) 1500 cm⁻¹; dominant CO₂ activation product on active catalyst under DRM at 600°C; stabilised by surface oxygen vacancies.

Bidentate carbonate at 1605 cm⁻¹ confirmed as active RWGS intermediate by ¹³C isotopic exchange at 200°C: ¹³CO₂ replaces ¹²C faster than the formate pool, indicating these carbonates are directly involved in the catalytic cycle.

bands.description: Bidentate carbonate symmetric stretch (b-CO₃²⁻*).

references.note: Table 3: νs(-C-O) at 1310 cm⁻¹; paired with the asymmetric modes at 1670/1560/1500 cm⁻¹.
Bidentate carbonate symmetric stretch at 1251 cm⁻¹; paired with ν_as at 1605 cm⁻¹ (Δν ≈ 354 cm⁻¹ consistent with bidentate coordination). ¹³C exchange confirms activity in RWGS.

bands.description: Bidentate carbonate asymmetric stretch first overtone (b-CO₃²⁻*); rare but reported.
Monodentate carbonate asymmetric stretch (m-CO₃²⁻*); small splitting (Δν ~100 cm⁻¹).

references.note: Table 3: νas(OCO⁻) at 1530 cm⁻¹; dominant CO₂ adsorption product on La-modified alumina; largely replaced by bidentate carbonate on active Ni-Ce-Fe/La-Al₂O₃.

bands.description: Monodentate carbonate symmetric stretch (m-CO₃²⁻*).

references.note: Table 3: νs(-C-O) at 1340 cm⁻¹.

bands.description: Monodentate carbonate asymmetric stretch first overtone (m-CO₃²⁻*); rare but reported.
Carbonate out-of-plane OCO bend / wagging (CO₃²⁻*); the central C moves out of the O-C-O plane. Position is general/approximate — not yet tied to a specific reference.
Carbonate in-plane OCO bend / scissoring (CO₃²⁻*); O-C-O angle deformation within the molecular plane. Position is general/approximate — not yet tied to a specific reference.
Bicarbonate asymmetric OCO stretch (HCO₃⁻*).

references.note: Table 3: δ(–OH) at 1650 cm⁻¹; formed by CO₂ interaction with surface OH groups; suppressed by La modification and Ni-Ce-Fe loading.

bands.description: Bicarbonate symmetric OCO stretch (HCO₃⁻*).

references.note: Table 3: νs(-C-O) at 1434 cm⁻¹; intense band confirming bicarbonate as the dominant CO₂ species on Al₂O₃.

bands.description: Bicarbonate COH bending (HCO₃⁻*); distinguishing feature vs. carbonate.

references.note: Table 3: δ(O-C-O) at 1200–1220 cm⁻¹.

bands.description: Formate C-H stretch (HCOO*); key HCOO* marker.

references.note: ν(CH) HCOO* on Cu⁺ at Cu–Ga₂O₃.

HCOO* ν(CH) at 2876 cm⁻¹; active intermediate confirmed by ME-DRIFTS-PSD during CO₂ hydrogenation (20 bar, 260°C). Also observed in small amounts on Cu-free GaZrOx via slow reduction of (bi)carbonates by Ga-H.

Lower arm of the formate ν(CH) Fermi resonance doublet at 2910 cm⁻¹ on CeO₂ (upper arm at 2945 cm⁻¹); ¹³C isotopic shift confirms C-H origin. Formate pool is large but exchanges more slowly than the bidentate carbonate pool, suggesting formate is not the primary RWGS active intermediate.

bands.description: Formate asymmetric OCO stretch (HCOO*); key HCOO* marker. Position is support-dependent: ~1520 cm⁻¹ on Ru/Al₂O₃ and Ru–Na₂O/Al₂O₃, shifting to ~1585–1600 cm⁻¹ on oxide-rich surfaces (Al₂O₃, CuGaZrOx). Appears during H₂ reduction as a methanation intermediate formed at the metal–support interface.

references.note: Table 2/Fig. 1a (Ru/Al₂O₃) and Fig. 3a (Ru–6.1%"Na₂O"/Al₂O₃ DFM): νas(OCO) HCOO* at 1520 cm⁻¹ on both surfaces, appearing at the onset of H₂ reduction (methanation step, 320 °C, 20% H₂/N₂). On Ru/Al₂O₃, formate forms via spillover of bicarbonates (adsorbed on Al₂O₃ OH groups); on Ru–Na₂O/Al₂O₃, it forms after bidentate carbonates (on Al-O⁻-Na⁺ sites) spill over to the Ru–support interface — same position despite the different CO₂ adsorption pathway. Confirmed reaction intermediate en route to CH₄.

νas(OCO) at 1600 cm⁻¹ (ME-DRIFTS, 20 bar, 260°C); confirmed active intermediate by CO₂ modulation-excitation PSD — responds at same frequency as product formation. Also at 1590 cm⁻¹ during methanol steam reforming on Cu-GaZrOx-24.
Table 3: νas(OCO⁻) at 1585 cm⁻¹; dominant CH₄ adsorption product on Al₂O₃ via H-abstraction; nearly absent on La-modified and Ni-Ce-Fe/La-Al₂O₃ under DRM.

Table 1, Fig. 6b–d: νas(OCO) of bidentate HCOO* resolved by p-polarized IRRAS (Fano line shape, UHV, room temperature). On Fe₃O₄(001) (Fig. 6c): two bidentate-bridging components, 1555 cm⁻¹ (tet site: oct-Fe above tet-Fe beneath) and 1548/1538 cm⁻¹ (p/s-pol; int site: oct-Fe above interstitial Fe) — paired νs(OCO) at 1369/1377 cm⁻¹ (tet/int); distinction only possible with polarized light due to Fano overlap in unpolarized spectra. On Fe₃O₄(111) (Fig. 6b/d): quasi-bidentate at 1588 cm⁻¹ (one O to Fe-tet, other to surface OH; paired νs at 1335 cm⁻¹, positive inverted Fano sign — TDM parallel to surface) and chelating at 1548 cm⁻¹ very weak (both O to single Fe-tet; paired νs at 1380 cm⁻¹); bidentate-bridging excluded here (Fe-tet neighbor distance 5.9 Å too large). Chelating forms first (from 0.05 L); quasi-bidentate develops above 0.2 L.

bands.description: Formate symmetric OCO stretch (HCOO*). Position varies with support and adsorption geometry: ~1320 cm⁻¹ on Ru/Al₂O₃, ~1335 cm⁻¹ (quasi-bidentate on Fe₃O₄(111)), ~1350–1380 cm⁻¹ on oxide surfaces (Al₂O₃, CuGaZrOx), ~1369–1377 cm⁻¹ on Fe₃O₄(001). Paired with νas(OCO) above ~1520 cm⁻¹; frequency splitting Δν = νas − νs reflects adsorption geometry (bridging vs. chelating).

references.note: Table 2/Fig. 1a (Ru/Al₂O₃) and Fig. 3a (Ru–6.1%"Na₂O"/Al₂O₃ DFM): νs(OCO) HCOO* at 1320 cm⁻¹ on both surfaces, paired with νas at 1520 cm⁻¹; appears at onset of H₂ reduction (320 °C, 20% H₂/N₂). On Ru/Al₂O₃, formate forms via bicarbonate spillover at the Ru–Al₂O₃ interface; on Ru–Na₂O/Al₂O₃, from bidentate carbonate spillover to the Ru–support interface. Identified as a key CO₂ methanation intermediate.

Table 1, Fig. 6a–d: νs(OCO) of bidentate HCOO* resolved by p-polarized IRRAS (negative Fano profiles, TDM perpendicular to surface; dissociative HCOOH adsorption, room temperature, UHV). On Fe₃O₄(001) (Fig. 6a/c): bidentate-bridging, two components — 1369 cm⁻¹ (tet site) and 1377 cm⁻¹ (int site), Epn coupling; paired νas(OCO) at 1555/1548 cm⁻¹ (tet/int); δ(CH) at 1373/1385 cm⁻¹ also observed with inverted Fano shape. On Fe₃O₄(111) (Fig. 6b/d): quasi-bidentate at 1335 cm⁻¹ (paired νas at 1588 cm⁻¹) and chelating at 1380 cm⁻¹ (paired νas at 1548 cm⁻¹); no bidentate-bridging here (Fe-tet spacing 5.9 Å too large). Chelating forms first (from 0.05 L); quasi-bidentate develops above 0.2 L.
νs(OCO) at ~1350 cm⁻¹ (Figure 1b, ME-DRIFTS, 20 bar, 260°C); companion band to νas at 1600 cm⁻¹.
Table 3: νs(OCO⁻) at 1380 cm⁻¹.

bands.description: Formate C-H bending (HCOO*); overlaps νₛ(OCO).

references.note: Formate C-H bending overlaps with νs(OCO) in the 1350–1400 cm⁻¹ region; formate confirmed as key intermediate in CO₂ hydrogenation at 20 bar, 260°C. Band not separately resolved from νs in this study.

bands.description: Formate combination band (HCOO*): bending + asymmetric stretch; diagnostic for HCOO*.

references.note: Formate combination band on Cu⁺ at Cu–Ga₂O₃.

Upper arm of the formate ν(CH) Fermi resonance doublet at 2945 cm⁻¹ on CeO₂ (lower arm at 2910 cm⁻¹). The ~35 cm⁻¹ doublet splitting is characteristic of HCOO* Fermi coupling between ν(CH) and 2δ(CH) or δ(OCH)+νₐₛ(OCO).

bands.description: Formate higher combination band (HCOO*); sometimes assigned as 2ν(C=O) overtone in older literature.

Methoxy CH₃ asymmetric stretch (CH₃O*). Position is support- and site-sensitive; frequency shifts between catalysts are diagnostic of a change in adsorption site. Distinguishable from coadsorbed CH₃OH(a), which is typically blue-shifted ~10–20 cm⁻¹.

references.note: Monodentate CH₃O* from CH₃OH dosing on anatase TiO₂.
ν_as(CH₃) on Cu⁺ at Cu–Ga₂O₃; downshifted from ~2926 cm⁻¹ on unpromoted Cu/SiO₂ — diagnostic of the Ga promoter-induced site change.
ν_as(CH₃) at 2970 cm⁻¹ on Zr⁴⁺ sites of Zr-rich CuGaZrOx.

bands.description: Methoxy CH₃ symmetric stretch (CH₃O*). Position is support- and site-sensitive, shifting in tandem with νₐₛ(CH₃). Often appears as a shoulder pair with coadsorbed CH₃OH(a) at ~10–20 cm⁻¹ higher frequency.

references.note: ν_s(CH₃) on Cu⁺ at Cu–Ga₂O₃; downshifted from ~2842 cm⁻¹ on unpromoted Cu/SiO₂ — mirrors the ν_as(CH₃) site-diagnostic shift.
ν_s(CH₃) at 2819 cm⁻¹ on Zr⁴⁺ sites of Zr-rich CuGaZrOx.

bands.description: Methoxy CH₃ asymmetric deformation (CH₃O*). Appears as a single resolved band, in contrast to ethoxy which shows separate δₛ and δₐₛ features. Largely geometry- and support-insensitive.

references.note: Table 3: δ(–CH₃) at 1480 cm⁻¹; surface methoxy deformation from CH₄ activation via H-abstraction; observed during DRM at 600°C.

bands.description: Methoxy CH₃ symmetric deformation (CH₃O*). Not always resolved as a separate band (e.g. Wu 2000 reports only the asymmetric deformation at 1441 on TiO₂); reported on other supports. May overlap with formate νₛ(OCO) at ~1365 cm⁻¹.
Monodentate methoxy C-O stretch (CH₃O* bonded via O to a single metal cation). Position is support-dependent. Diagnostic threshold: ν(C-O) > ~1100 cm⁻¹ indicates monodentate geometry (Hussein 1991).

references.note: Sub-components at 1100/1126/1156 cm⁻¹ reflecting a distribution of monodentate sites; dominates over bidentate ~3:1 by integrated area; ~1.5× higher photoreactivity toward HCOO* than bidentate.
Zr-OCH₃ species: methoxy coordinated to Zr⁴⁺ sites on CuGaZrOx at 1152 cm⁻¹.

bands.description: Bidentate methoxy C-O stretch (CH₃O* bridging two metal cations, or bonded at a bridging-O vacancy). Diagnostic threshold: ν(C-O) < ~1100 cm⁻¹ indicates bidentate geometry (Hussein 1991). Overlaps closely with methanol ν(C-O) at ~1030 cm⁻¹ — distinguish via the absence of the CH₃OH(a) νₛ(CH₃) marker at higher frequency.

references.note: Similar thermal stability to monodentate (no interconversion ≤ 300 °C); ~1.5× lower photoreactivity toward HCOO* than monodentate.

bands.description: Methanol O-H stretch (MeOH*/MeOH(g)); often obscured by adsorbed water and support hydroxyls.

Adsorbed methanol CH₃ asymmetric stretch (CH₃OH*). Typically blue-shifted ~10–20 cm⁻¹ relative to methoxy νₐₛ(CH₃); the cleanest C-H region marker to distinguish molecularly-adsorbed methanol from methoxy.

references.note: Removed by evacuation at 200 °C, leaving methoxy on the surface.

bands.description: Adsorbed methanol CH₃ symmetric stretch (CH₃OH*). Typically blue-shifted ~10–20 cm⁻¹ from methoxy νₛ(CH₃). Appears as a shoulder pair with methoxy; mild evacuation selectively removes CH₃OH* and leaves methoxy as the dominant feature.

Methanol C-O stretch (MeOH*/MeOH(g)). Falls in the 1000–1200 cm⁻¹ window shared with monodentate and bidentate methoxy ν(C-O); CH₃OH(a) and CH₃O(a) routinely coexist after low-temperature alcohol dosing and contribute jointly to this region. Disambiguate via the CH₃ stretching region: adsorbed methanol shows νₐₛ/νₛ blue-shifted by ~10–20 cm⁻¹ relative to methoxy.
Sharp band; isolated terminal hydroxyls on metal-oxide supports.
Broader band; bridged or hydrogen-bonded hydroxyls.
Very broad O-H stretch of adsorbed/condensed water (H₂O*).
Water bending mode (H₂O*); overlaps formate νₐₛ.
Gallium hydride (Ga-H*) on Ga₂O₃-based catalysts; marker for heterolytic H₂ dissociation. Confirmed by D₂ isotope shift. Plays a role in converting HCOO* to CH₃O* via H spillover.

references.note: Ga-H at 1976 cm⁻¹; confirmed by D₂ substitution (isotope shift observed). Present on GaZrOx and CuGaZrOx under CO₂/H₂ at 20 bar, 260°C. Partially static during MES — consistent with slow HCOO* → CH₃O* conversion.
